actions.description: CPU use of each track (and the master, `track` null) and of each insert on it, averaged over the last half second of processing (`window`, seconds): `per_buffer_us` (microseconds per audio buffer), `share` (that time over the buffer's duration, its deadline: 1 is all of it) and `buffers` measured. A track's figure is all its work (clips, inserts, fader, sends); its inserts are listed most costly first, and the tracks too. Tracks run in parallel on the audio threads, so shares can add up past 1 without a dropout; get_stats has the overall DSP load. Every track and insert keeps running while stopped, so effects' tails and monitoring work: the numbers are not zero then. Each insert's `misses` counts the blocks it has missed since it loaded (its track silent for that block) because its plug-in was held elsewhere when the audio thread came for it. instructions: Controls the running DAW. Start with get_project to learn track, clip and insert ids; positions are in samples at the project's sample rate. screenshot shows the window as the user sees it. MIDI is in ticks (960 per quarter note) or "bar:beat:tick" from 1: describe_midi_clip reads a clip as music (key, chords, note names), add_notes takes those forms back, and the write_midi_part prompt walks through writing a part. search_manual answers "how do I…" from Oxide's manual, and open_manual shows the user a page of it.

prompts.name: write_midi_part
prompts.text:
Write a lead melody in Oxide that fits the MIDI clip it should fit (find it in get_project).

1. Read the song. get_project lists the tracks with their MIDI clips (ids, start and length in ticks, 960 per quarter note), the tempo and time signature; get_tempo_map gives every change. describe_midi_clip on the clip gives its key (with the runner-up and their scores), scale, chords bar by bar (`progression`, `chords` with their tones), the tempo and meter where it plays, its range, and every note's song position `at` ("bar:beat:tick", from 1) and name (C4 = 60).
2. Plan the part over the same bars: keep to the key's scale, put chord tones on the strong beats and passing notes between, phrase in two- or four-bar units, and keep its register clear of the clip's range (a melody an octave or more above a bass line). If the key's score is close to the runner-up's, let the chords decide.
3. Make a track for it: insert_midi_track with `bar` and `bars` (the clip's span), `after` (the clip's track) and `instrument` (an installed instrument from list_plugins); it returns the track and an empty clip over those bars. Or add_track (kind "instrument"), add_insert for the instrument, then add_midi_clip with `bar` and `bars`.
4. Write the notes with add_notes: `at` as "bar:beat:tick" ("5:1:000", "5:2:480"), `pitch` as a name ("E5", "Bb4"), `length` in ticks (960 a quarter note, 480 an eighth, 1920 a half), `velocity` 1-127 for accents. Every call is one undo step.
